channel.title: n8n release notes: editor and nodes
channel.description: Feature-level updates from n8n releases: what shipped in the editor and the integration nodes.

item.title: Restyle AI Assistant tab bar and add a tab hover card
item.description: Redesigned the AI Assistant's preview tab bar with an updated look, and added a hover card for each tab. The card shows the tab's full name, and for workflows also displays the last edited time and a Published/Draft status, while data table tabs show the edited time and column count. Details load efficiently via batched requests and refresh in the background. Closing tabs and the new tab button are not yet included.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Rename to Azure AI Foundry Chat Model
item.description: The 'Azure OpenAI Chat Model' node has been renamed to 'Azure AI Foundry Chat Model' to better reflect that it supports the full Azure AI Foundry catalogue (including Llama, Mistral, Cohere, DeepSeek, Grok and Claude models), not just OpenAI models. Existing workflows are unaffected, and searching for 'Azure OpenAI' still finds the node thanks to a new alias.

item.title: Improve Agent Builder intro interactions
item.description: The Agent Builder intro's template list has been refined: rows now use accessible, semantic markup with keyboard support (Tab, Enter, Space), a hover-revealed arrow indicator, subtle staged fade-and-blur animation, and cleaner spacing and text sizing. Redundant action buttons were removed since rows themselves are now clickable, improving usability for both mouse and keyboard/screen-reader users.

item.title: Group canvas toolbar buttons in a single container
item.description: The canvas toolbar buttons—zoom controls (bottom-left) and canvas actions (top-right)—are now grouped into a single visual container with a shared background, rounded corners, and shadow, instead of appearing as separate floating buttons. This saves canvas space and gives a cleaner, more unified look in both the editor and the node creator panel, in light and dark mode.

item.title: Animate height changes in the MCP callback URLs dialog
item.description: The Allowed callback URLs dialog under Settings → Instance-level MCP now animates smoothly instead of jumping. Switching between 'All callback URLs' and 'Only trusted URLs', adding or removing a URL row, and validation messages appearing all transition with a smooth grow/shrink motion. Reduced motion settings are respected, showing a simple fade instead. No functional or validation behavior changes.

item.title: Preview own connected clients on the MCP settings overview
item.description: The instance-level MCP settings overview now previews your first three connected clients directly, showing brand, client type, connection time, and access summary, with a hover-revealed revoke action. A 'View all' row appears only when more clients exist. The clients page's owner column is now more compact and the revoke button is properly right-aligned.

item.title: Displays instance admins (and owner) in all project user lists
item.description: Project member lists now always show instance owners and admins with a 'full access' role and explanatory tooltip, since they already have implicit access to all projects. They can't be removed or edited, and are excluded from the user picker when adding members. Related API endpoints now reject edits/removals of instance admins and ignore them in add requests. Also adds pagination and search to project member lists.

item.title: Make SSO the primary option on the sign-in page when SSO is enabled
item.description: When SAML or OIDC is the active login method, the sign-in page now leads with a Continue with SSO button, with the email/password form collapsed behind a disclosure (still accessible via a recovery query parameter). If password sign-in is refused because SSO is required, an inline callout with its own SSO action appears instead of a toast. Redirects after login, including on OIDC, now correctly return users to their original destination, with hardened validation against unsafe redirect URLs. Instances without SSO are unaffected.

item.title: Add Mistral Vibe to the MCP connect-client picker
item.description: Instance-level MCP settings now let you connect Mistral Vibe from the "Connect a client" picker, listed under Web alongside ChatGPT. Selecting it opens Vibe's connector marketplace on a preset n8n template; users paste their server URL and complete OAuth consent. Vibe also gets its own brand icon, and connected Vibe clients now show the Mistral logo and assistant type in the connected-clients table instead of a generic icon.

item.title: Add Gateway credits option to Agent web search
item.description: Agents can now pay for web search using Gateway credits, the same way they already can for models and tools. When Brave Search is served through the AI Gateway, the web search credential picker offers a managed "Gateway credits" option with a balance indicator, so no personal Brave API key is needed. This option is not available for SearXNG, which the gateway does not support.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Send activity feed notifications to a user
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports sending activity feed notifications to a user via a new Activity Notification resource with a Send operation. It works with OAuth2, Microsoft, and Service Principal credentials, validates the Topic Link, and surfaces clear errors when the companion Teams app isn't installed or required permissions are missing. Existing OAuth2 credentials must be reconnected to pick up the new scope.

item.title: Use test label and icon for agent preview
item.description: In the AI agent builder, the preview action has been relabeled as "Test agent" with a flask icon replacing the previous play icon, better reflecting its purpose. The close button for the test panel now has an updated accessible label, "Hide test", improving clarity for screen reader users.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add online meeting attendees on Create, Create or Get and Update
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Online Meeting resource now supports Attendees on Create, Create or Get, and Update. Pick people via the shared user picker or supply IDs/emails by expression, with an optional Attendee/Presenter role on Create and Update. Allowed Presenters gains a Specific People option. Update replaces the full attendee list; an empty list clears attendees. Requires User.Read.All permission for lookups.

item.title: Anthropic Node: Add prompt caching to the Message operation
item.description: The Anthropic node's Text → Message operation now supports a Prompt Caching option (Disabled, 5 Minutes, or 1 Hour), matching the Anthropic Chat Model sub-node. When enabled, requests include a cache breakpoint so repeated tool-call loops and large system prompts are billed at reduced rates for cached tokens. Reported token usage now correctly includes cache creation and read tokens. Disabled by default, so existing workflows are unaffected.

item.title: Move agent skills to a separate card
item.description: In the AI Agent builder, Skills now appear in their own dedicated card below Model and Instructions, labeled with the subtitle "How this agent handles specific tasks". Previously grouped within the Capabilities section, Skills are now easier to find and manage as a distinct part of agent configuration.

item.title: Show timestamp dividers in the agent preview chat
item.description: The agent preview chat now shows timestamp dividers above messages, so it's clear when a conversation happened. A divider appears above the first user message and again whenever more than an hour passes or the calendar day changes, labeled as "Today at HH:MM", "Yesterday at HH:MM", or a full date, formatted in the viewer's locale. Older history without a saved timestamp simply shows no divider.

item.title: Databricks Node: Show the Chat Model node in the node picker
item.description: The Databricks Chat Model node is now visible in the node picker when adding a Chat Model to AI Agent or Basic LLM Chain nodes. Previously the node existed but was hidden while it was being finalized. Existing workflows already using this node are unaffected.

item.title: Move web search to agent capabilities
item.description: Web search settings for agents have moved from the Advanced settings panel to the Capabilities card, where it now appears as its own capability row. Native provider options (for models like OpenAI and Anthropic) and fallback providers (Brave, SearXNG) with their credential selectors are still available, just relocated for easier discovery when configuring an agent's capabilities.

item.title: Make view related tag permissions available by default
item.description: Custom instance roles now include a 'Tags: View' permission by default, letting all users view and select existing tags on workflows even without tag management rights. Previously this was bundled with 'Manage', requiring extra permissions just to see tags. The tag picker now clearly indicates when a user lacks permission to create new tags. Note: existing custom roles created before this change won't automatically get the new scope.

item.title: Distinguish skills from tools in session timelines
item.description: Agent session timelines now distinguish skill calls from regular tool calls, showing them with a dedicated 'Skill' label, a book icon, and an orange color. Node rows in the timeline also display the actual configured node icon when available. Skill events can be filtered, searched, and inspected in the detail panel showing their input and output, making it easier to trace agent behavior.

item.title: MiniMax Node: Fetch available models from the API instead of a hardcoded list
item.description: The MiniMax and MiniMax Chat Model nodes now fetch available models directly from the MiniMax API instead of relying on a hardcoded list, so new models appear automatically. The Model field (version 1.2) offers a searchable, credential-aware list plus an option to enter a custom model ID. Existing workflows keep their prior node version and static model list unchanged.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add [@mention](https://github.com/mention) support to message Create
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports @mentions when creating channel or chat messages. Add one or more mentions via a new user picker (search by list, ID, or email), and n8n resolves each user against Microsoft Graph so mentions render as real chips and trigger the recipient's Teams notification, instead of appearing as plain, inert text.

item.title: Mark required agent fields
item.description: The agent editor now marks the Model and Instructions fields with a red asterisk to indicate they are required, matching the convention used elsewhere in n8n forms. This is a copy-only UI update to improve clarity; no functional or validation changes were made.

item.title: Split workflows into a separate capability row
item.description: In the agent builder, workflow tools now appear in their own Workflows row, separate from other tools. The Add tool and Add workflow buttons open dedicated pickers scoped to the relevant item types, so tool search shows only tools and workflow search shows only workflows. The workflow picker also includes a search placeholder and the ability to create a new workflow directly from the picker.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the channel message undo delete operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports an Undo Delete operation for channel messages and replies, letting you restore a previously deleted message via the Graph undoSoftDelete action. It returns { success: true } on completion. This operation is unavailable when using the Service Principal credential, where the related fields are hidden and a notice is shown.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the channel message delete operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports a Delete operation for channel messages and replies, calling Microsoft Graph's soft delete endpoint. This requires the ChannelMessage.ReadWrite OAuth2 scope; existing credentials keep their original scopes, so users must create a new credential or enable Custom Scopes and add ChannelMessage.ReadWrite to use it. Delete is not available with Service Principal credentials.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the chat message undo delete operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node (v2) now supports an Undo Delete operation for chat messages, letting you restore a message previously removed with the Delete operation by providing the same chat and message ID. This operation is available with OAuth2 credentials but is not supported when using a Service Principal credential.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the chat message delete operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Chat Message resource now supports a Delete operation. Provide a chat and message ID to soft-delete a message you sent; n8n resolves the signed-in user and calls the Microsoft Graph softDelete action, returning a success confirmation. Deleted messages remain recoverable via a future undo operation. This operation is not available when using the Service Principal credential.

item.title: Confluence Node: Unhide the node and enable AI tool usage
item.description: The Confluence node is now publicly available in the nodes panel and search, no longer hidden behind a feature flag. It can also be used as a tool by AI Agents, allowing agents to create, read, and manage Confluence pages directly within workflows.

item.title: Show background tasks in the agent preview
item.description: The agent preview now shows a live panel of background tasks (sub-agents and workflow jobs) above the composer, with running and recently finished jobs grouped together. The panel stays visible until results reach chat, supports keyboard-accessible expansion, and shows a persistent 'Background task results received' entry in the conversation when background work resumes a parent turn. Requires enabling the agents module and background tasks setting.

item.title: AI Agent Node: Add option to force a tool call on the first iteration
item.description: The AI Agent node (v3) and Agent Tool (v3) now include an opt-in 'Force Tool Call on First Iteration' option. When enabled, the model must call a tool on its first response of a run, helping smaller or less compliant models (e.g. Mistral-Small on IONOS, vLLM, Ollama) that otherwise reply in prose and skip wired tools. Later iterations remain unrestricted so the agent can still give a final answer. Default is off, so existing behavior is unchanged unless enabled.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the Service Principal path for Online Meeting Update
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports the Update operation for online meetings when using a Service Principal (app-only) credential, letting you update a meeting's subject and other fields by ID or join URL while specifying the organizer. All five online meeting operations are now available for both OAuth2 and Service Principal credentials, and the credential description no longer states that online meetings are unavailable.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the Service Principal path for Online Meeting Delete
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports deleting online meetings when using a Service Principal credential, identifying the meeting by ID or by join URL. Previously, this operation was only available with delegated (user) credentials. The createOrGet operation is also now available under Service Principal credentials.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the Service Principal path for Online Meeting Create or Get
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Online Meeting 'Create or Get' operation now works with Service Principal credentials, in addition to delegated auth. Using the same External ID for the same organizer returns the existing meeting instead of creating a duplicate; a different organizer creates a new meeting. The field description has been updated to clarify this behavior.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the Service Principal path for Online Meeting Get
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports the Get operation for Online Meetings when using a Service Principal (Entra) credential, retrieving a meeting by its ID or join URL from the organizer's meetings. Error messages when a meeting isn't found now reference both the Meeting and Organizer fields to help troubleshoot.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the Service Principal path for Online Meeting Create
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports creating online meetings using the Service Principal (app-only) credential. A new Organizer field lets you pick or enter the user on whose behalf the meeting is created, and the Operation list under this credential only shows supported actions, currently Create. Error messages now clarify required permissions (OnlineMeetings.ReadWrite.All, User.Read.All) and the Teams application access policy commands needed when Graph returns a 403.

item.title: Databricks Node: Append a per-row MCP registry attribution to the agent reply
item.description: MCP registry rows can now define an 'attribution' string that is appended to an AI Agent's final reply whenever a tool from that registry entry was used, satisfying partner requirements like Databricks' 'Powered by Genie' label. The label appears on a new blank line after the answer, works in streaming mode, avoids duplication if the model already included it, and is skipped when a structured output parser is used. Only applies to Agent V3 and registry-backed MCP tools; rows without attribution behave unchanged.

item.title: Hand agent change requests in the preview chat to the n8n Assistant
item.description: In the agent preview chat, the agent now recognizes it cannot change its own setup (instructions, model, tools, skills, knowledge, channels, integrations, schedules, or name) and tells users to use the n8n Assistant instead. When a message asks for such a change, the chat displays a note with a button that opens the n8n Assistant with the request pre-filled and the session attached. This behavior is limited to the preview chat and does not affect published channels, evals, MCP, or other test surfaces.

item.title: Add preview chat utilities to the more options menu
item.description: The agent preview chat panel now has a clearer close button plus a new more-options menu, replacing the confusing layout icon. The menu offers copy link, copy conversation, open in new tab, full width toggle, session deletion, optional LangSmith export, and session details like source, token usage, cost, duration, and last message time.

item.title: Azure Storage Node: Add Azure cloud selection and custom endpoints to the Shared Key credential
item.description: The Azure Storage Shared Key credential now has an Azure Cloud dropdown to select Azure Public Cloud, Azure US Government, Azure China, or Custom. Custom reveals an Endpoint field for private endpoints or custom domains, letting each credential target a different endpoint instead of relying on a single instance-wide override. Custom endpoints must be enabled by an administrator via the new N8N_AZURE_STORAGE_CUSTOM_ENDPOINTS_ENABLED setting (default off); otherwise custom credentials fail with a clear error. Existing credentials keep working unchanged, defaulting to the public cloud. Only host-style endpoints are supported; path-style endpoints are a future improvement.

item.title: Databricks Node: Send partner User-Agent on Genie MCP traffic
item.description: Databricks Genie MCP requests, along with other Databricks node traffic, now include a dedicated 'n8n_DatabricksNode' User-Agent header, letting Databricks correctly attribute activity to n8n in their audit logs. MCP registry remotes can now define custom headers that are sent on every request, and these now correctly survive OAuth token refreshes rather than being dropped.

item.title: Rename AI Assistant to n8n Assistant
item.description: The AI Assistant feature is now called "n8n Assistant" throughout the product, including UI labels, settings pages, error and log messages, agent panel text, and telemetry event descriptions. New model, web search, and sandbox connections created in Settings are named accordingly (e.g. "n8n Assistant model"); existing connections keep their current names. This is a naming-only change with no functional impact.

item.title: Replace Git connection CLI commands with Promotions
item.description: The CLI's git-connections commands are replaced by new promotion-provider and promotion-connection command groups, supporting provider and connection setup, directional (apply/promote) configuration, project links, clone, disconnect, and Promote/Apply operations, with JSON input via --stdin or --file. Additionally, single-object table output (e.g. workflow get, credential get) now displays long strings in full instead of truncating them, so values like SSH public keys can be copied completely.

item.title: Add workflow dependencies submenu to the workflow menu
item.description: The workflow menu now includes a Dependencies entry when a workflow uses credentials, sub-workflows, or other linked resources. Its submenu lists dependencies grouped by type; selecting a credential opens it in the credential modal, while sub-workflows and other workflow dependencies open in a new tab. The entry is hidden for workflows without dependencies or unsaved new workflows.

item.title: Databricks Node: Refresh user-login tokens in the chat model during long executions
item.description: The Databricks node's chat model now supports OAuth2 User-Login (Authorization Code) credentials, in addition to service-principal credentials. Previously, long-running executions using a user-login credential would fail once the access token expired mid-run. The node now checks token expiry before each request and refreshes it automatically, retrying failed requests after a refresh. If the session truly can't be renewed, users get a clear message telling them to reconnect their credential instead of a raw 403 error.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the chat member remove operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Chat Member resource now supports a Remove operation, letting you remove a member from a group chat. A member picker lets you select the person to remove without needing to know their membership ID. Attempts to remove a member from a one-on-one chat or the last owner of a group chat return a clear error explaining why.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add the chat member add operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports adding a member to a group chat via a new Chat Member 'Add' operation. Users are selected from an org-wide picker or entered by ID, with options to set the member's role and how much chat history they can see. The chat and user pickers used across Chat Member, Chat Message, and the Teams trigger also now return more results.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add Online Meeting Create or Get operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Online Meeting resource now supports a Create or Get operation. Given an External ID, it creates a new meeting on first run and returns the existing meeting on subsequent runs, preventing duplicates when workflows re-execute. Subject, Start Time and End Time are optional; invalid combinations (like an End Time without a Start Time) or a blank External ID are caught before any request is sent.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add Online Meeting Update operation
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Online Meeting resource now supports an Update operation, letting you change subject, start/end time, and meeting settings (camera, mic, chat mode, reactions, presenters, entry announcement, lobby bypass scope, auto-recording) by meeting ID or join URL. Start and end times must be updated together, and Lobby Bypass Scope gains Invited and Organization Excluding Guests options, also now available on Create. Require Passcode remains unavailable on Update since Graph disallows changing it after creation.

item.title: Add manual agent creation entry point on the agents pages
item.description: On the agents pages, when Instance AI is set up, the create-agent dropdown now includes a 'Create agent manually' option that opens the standalone agent builder directly on an unsaved draft, bypassing the Instance AI assisted creation flow. The main Create agent button still launches Instance AI when available, or falls back to the manual builder when it isn't.
